newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian '97 deficit seen below 2.9% of GDP - paper.
newsitem.headline: Belgian '97 deficit seen below 2.9% of GDP - paper.

text.p: Belgium's 1997 public sector deficit is likely to be lower than the 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP) government target, National Bank governor Alfons Verplaetse was quoted on Thursday as saying.
De Financieel Economische Tijd newspaper quoted him as telling a conference on the euro in Genval, southern Belgium, that the deficit would be between 2.6 and 2.9 percent of GDP.
The Belgian government said early this month its 1997 budget would cut the deficit to 2.9 percent from an estimated 3.3 percent in 1996.
Belgium had to cut its budget deficit to below three percent of GDP in 1997 if it wanted to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU).
The Tijd said Verplaetse did not say why he was optimistic, but he suggested that the basis assumptions for economic growth and interest rates in the budget were very cautious.
It said previous governments had been less cautious and inclined to underestimate the deficit.
"In the past, a deficit of 2.6 percent would have been published," Verplaetse was quoted as saying.
